standard: Session log of a zone-based firewall (traffic log written when a session ends, or when a packet is dropped); column names are plain
notes: All times UTC with a Z suffix. Sampling follows the Zeek logs: traffic that people cause is a 1-in-200 sample; machine-generated periodic traffic, sessions through the remote-access gateway and the employee VPN, and the flows behind an alert or an audit record are recorded in full. One record for every Zeek flow that crosses the device; dropped inbound internet traffic is a sample. Hosts are joined by address to 06_data_streams/gw_host_registry.json. External addresses and names are invented. Two devices: GW-FW-EDGE-01 (internet edge) and GW-OT-FW-01 (boundary between the corporate network, the IT/OT DMZ and the control network). A flow that passes both appears in both; flows that stay inside the corporate network or inside the control network pass neither. Addresses are those on the inside of the device: for inbound flows dst_ip is the internal address of the published service; for dropped inbound packets it is the public address they were sent to. Byte counters count whole IP packets (headers included) and equal orig_ip_bytes / resp_ip_bytes of the flow in conn.log. While the control network is cut off, the boundary firewall allows nothing across and logs what was refused. Public block 12.186.44.64/28: .65 firewall, .66-.69 outbound source NAT, .70 mail gateway, .71 public website, .72 customer portal, .73 external DNS, .74 file transfer, .75 employee VPN, .76 OT remote-access gateway.

sessions.description: One row per session or dropped packet, in time order. A session is filed under the month in which it ended.

fields.name: time_utc
fields.notes: When the record was written: session end for allowed sessions (start = time_utc - duration_s), arrival time for drops

fields.name: src_zone
fields.notes: zone in gw_host_registry.json network_zones, or internet

fields.name: app
fields.notes: Application the device identified (ssl, web-browsing, smtp, dns, ntp, ms-rdp, ms-ds-smb, historian-data, dnp3, modbus-tcp, ms-update ...); incomplete when a TCP handshake did not finish; not-applicable for drops

fields.name: bytes_sent
fields.notes: IP bytes from the source, headers included (packet size for drops); equals orig_ip_bytes in conn.log

fields.name: bytes_recv
fields.notes: IP bytes from the destination, headers included; equals resp_ip_bytes in conn.log; 0 for drops

fields.name: duration_s
fields.notes: Session length in seconds (0 for drops)

fields.name: nat_src_ip
fields.notes: Public source address after translation, outbound sessions on the edge only
